Pegasus · Upload design review · 25 September 2026

From files to the right Case.

Five new, interactive proposals. A quieter hierarchy, useful photographic previews and one explicit Case decision throughout. Each includes the full journey from selection to outcome, with the earlier five versions kept alongside for comparison.

Back to the v30 walkthrough

See the decision clearly

Case, registration, claimant, Principal and Case/PO appear together. A possible match is never automatically selected.

Make the files useful

Real preview interactions, readable names, compact outcomes and a marked unreadable file. Eleven long filenames exercise every layout.

Finish with certainty

Review the exact Case before adding. Failures preserve the decision; success names the confirmed destination.

The strongest everyday balance. Case identity and the complete file roster stay together in one work surface.

Contact sheet

Recognise the evidence before choosing its home.

Large, real image previews make a photographic upload easy to recognise. A steady Case panel stays beside the gallery.

Compact ledger

The whole upload, in a single scan.

A horizontal Case decision above precise, compact file rows. Best for large batches, mixed formats and repeated office use.

Tradeoff · Small thumbnails provide less image detail without opening a preview.

E

Inspection studio

Look closely. Keep the Case in view.

A large photograph, a selectable file rail and the Case decision form a dedicated review workspace.

Tradeoff · Uses the most screen space; narrower windows stack the photograph below the decision.

Explore Inspection studio →Start with file selectionEarlier E
My recommendation: A — Review desk. It gives the Case decision a clear home and keeps the complete file roster in view. C is the strongest visual option for image-heavy work; D is the most efficient for repeated batch review.
Try it: select a Case, review, cancel, choose another Case, open a file or search for “Morgan”, “QDOS25802” or “26018”. Open Mockup controls for all 20 states, sample file selection and a confirmation conflict.
